scenes.title: The Big Number Mystery
narration: Have you ever wondered how much a brand new car costs in rupees?
It might cost 8,50,000 rupees, which is a very large number!
Today we will learn how to read and understand these giant numbers.

scenes.title: Understanding Place Value
narration: Every digit in a number has a special home called a place value.
Starting from the right, we have ones, tens, and hundreds.
Next come thousands, ten thousands, and lakhs.
Where a digit sits tells us exactly how much it is worth.

scenes.title: Breaking Down 8,50,000
narration: Let's look at our 8,50,000 rupees again.
The 8 is in the lakh place, so it means 8 lakhs.
The 5 is in the ten thousands place, meaning 50,000.
Together, they add up to make the full value of the number.

scenes.title: Quick Recap
narration: Remember, digits change value based on where they are sitting.
Always use commas to group numbers into thousands and lakhs.
Think about it, what is the biggest number you can write using five digits?

scenes.title: The Big Candy Problem
narration: Aarav has 75 yummy mango candies to share equally among 5 friends.
How many candies does each friend get without any leftovers?
We use long division to solve this big problem step by step.

scenes.title: Step by Step Division
narration: First, see how many times 5 goes into the tens digit, which is 7.
5 fits into 7 one time, so we write 1 on top.
Multiply 1 times 5 and subtract it from 7 to get 2.
Now, bring down the 5 from the ones place to make 25.

scenes.title: Completing the Share
narration: Now divide 25 by 5 to find our final answer.
Since 5 times 5 is 25, we write 5 on top.
Subtract 25 from 25, and we have 0 left over.

scenes.title: Recap and Challenge
narration: We divided, multiplied, subtracted, and brought down to get 15.
Each friend gets 15 delicious mango candies to enjoy.
Think about it: what would happen if we had 76 candies instead?

scenes.title: The Curious Cookie Riddle
narration: Imagine Priya has seven delicious ladoos on her plate today.
Can she share them equally with her friends without breaking any?
Let us see if we can arrange these numbers into perfect rows.

scenes.title: What Makes a Prime?
narration: A prime number is a special number that only has two factors.
It can only be divided by the number one and itself.
If you try to make groups with other numbers, you always get leftovers.

scenes.title: Testing the Number Five
narration: Let us test the number five to see if it is prime.
We can make one row of five or five rows of one.
But we cannot divide five into two or three equal groups.
Because five has only two factors, it is definitely a prime number.

scenes.title: Recap and Challenge
narration: Remember, prime numbers are lonely numbers that only share with one and themselves.
Numbers like four or six are not prime because they have more factors.
Think about it: is the number eleven a prime number or not?

scenes.title: The Big Shopping Trip
narration: Imagine we buy 12 packets of yummy mango sweets at 25 rupees each.
How do we find the total cost without counting every single rupee?
Multiplication helps us solve this big problem quickly and easily.

scenes.title: Breaking Down the Numbers
narration: First, we write 25 and 12 one above the other carefully.
We multiply the top number by the ones place first.
Then, we multiply by the tens place, adding a zero placeholder.
Always remember to carry over any extra tens to the next column.

scenes.title: Solving the Mango Problem
narration: Two times 25 gives us 50 for the ones part.
Ten times 25 gives us 250 for the tens part.
Finally, we add 50 and 250 together to get 300.

scenes.title: Quick Recap and Challenge
narration: Multiply ones, then multiply tens with a zero, then add both parts.
You can multiply any big number using these simple steps.
Think about it: how much would 15 notebooks cost if each is 40 rupees?

scenes.title: The Sweet Sharing Mystery
narration: Aarav has 12 ladoos to share equally with his friends.
How can he group them without leaving any behind?
Let us discover how numbers work together.

scenes.title: Finding Hidden Factors
narration: Factors are numbers that divide another number perfectly.
For 12, the factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 12.
Notice how they always come in pairs.

scenes.title: Making Giant Multiples
narration: Multiples are what we get when we multiply numbers.
Think of multiples like skipping numbers on a line.
A multiple of 3 keeps growing bigger forever.

scenes.title: Reviewing Our Math Skills
narration: Factors are small and fixed, multiples are big and endless.
Remember, factors divide, but multiples multiply.
Think about it: Is 5 a factor or a multiple of 20?

scenes.title: The Sweet Snack Hook
narration: Aarav is packing his tiffin for school today.
He has two samosas and three ladoos.
How can we describe this mix of snacks using numbers?

scenes.title: Understanding Ratio Basics
narration: A ratio shows how much of one thing we have compared to another.
We write it with a special colon symbol like this.
The order of numbers matters a lot.

scenes.title: Working The Samosa Ratio
narration: Aarav has two samosas for every three ladoos.
So the ratio of samosas to ladoos is two to three.
If he doubles his snacks, the ratio stays the same.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Ratios compare parts of a group using a colon.
Remember to keep the same order as the objects.
Think about it: If you have four pens and two pencils, what is your ratio?

scenes.title: Shapes in Your Home
narration: Have you noticed how your sandwich is a square and your bowl is a circle?
Geometry is just the study of these shapes and how they fit together perfectly.
Why do builders use triangles to make roofs strong instead of squares?

scenes.title: Understanding Geometry Basics
narration: A point is just a tiny dot marking a spot in space.
When you connect two points, you get a straight line.
When lines meet at a corner, they create an angle.
Closed shapes made of straight lines are called polygons.

scenes.title: Measuring a Rectangle
narration: Let us find the area of a rectangular table top in your room.
First, measure the length which is 10 cm.
Next, measure the width which is 5 cm.
Multiply 10 by 5 to get 50 square centimeters of space.

scenes.title: Recap and Challenge
narration: Geometry helps us measure points, lines, angles, and shapes all around us.
Remember, area is just the space inside a flat shape.
Think about it, why do you think wheels are always circles instead of squares?

scenes.title: The Big Sale Hook
narration: Aarav sees a store sign saying 50 percent off his favorite toy cricket bat.
He wonders what percent actually means when buying toys with his pocket money.
Let us discover how percentages help us understand parts of a whole.

scenes.title: What is a Percent
narration: Percent simply means out of one hundred.
Think of a hundred rupee note made of one hundred small coins.
If you have twenty coins, that is twenty out of one hundred.
In math language, we call this twenty percent.

scenes.title: Solving a Discount Example
narration: Aarav's cricket bat costs two hundred rupees.
The store offers a fifty percent discount, which is half the price.
Fifty percent of two hundred rupees is exactly one hundred rupees.

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Percentages always compare a number to one hundred.
They help us compare deals, marks, and parts of things easily.
Think about it: If you eat ten percent of a pizza, how much is left?

scenes.title: Where is the hidden toy
narration: Have you ever played a game of hide and seek with your toys?
Imagine Priya hid her teddy bear inside a large floor grid.
How can we tell exactly where the bear is hiding?

scenes.title: The Magic of Coordinates
narration: We use two lines to map out our space.
The horizontal line is the x-axis, going left to right.
The vertical line is the y-axis, going up and down.
Together, they help us find any spot using two numbers.

scenes.title: Mapping Priya's Teddy Bear
narration: Start at the corner, which is zero zero.
Move three steps to the right along the x-axis.
Now move two steps up the y-axis.
We found the bear at point three, two!

scenes.title: Quick Review
narration: Always walk along the floor before you climb the wall.
Coordinates are just a secret address for any spot.
Think about it: where would you place a snack on a grid?

scenes.title: Sharing A Delicious Pizza
narration: Arjun bought a large pizza to share with his best friend Meera.
But how can they split it so they both get an equal amount?
Fractions help us divide things into equal parts.

scenes.title: Understanding The Parts
narration: The bottom number is the denominator, showing the total number of slices.
The top number is the numerator, showing how many slices you take.
So one slice out of four is written as one-fourth.
The line between them acts like a division sign.

scenes.title: Counting Real Rupees
narration: Imagine you have ten rupees and you give half to your brother.
Half of ten is five rupees, because ten divided by two is five.
Fractions work for money just like they work for pizza slices.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Fractions show parts of a whole, like a yummy pizza.
Think about it, if you have a chocolate bar with six squares, what is two-sixths?

scenes.title: The Big Box Question
narration: Have you ever wondered how much space is inside your school tiffin box?
Let us explore why we need to measure the surface and the space inside.
We use area for flat shapes and volume for things that hold stuff.

scenes.title: Understanding Area and Volume
narration: Area is how much flat space a shape covers, measured in square centimeters.
To find area, multiply the length by the width.
Volume is how much space an object takes up in three dimensions.
Volume is length times width times height.

scenes.title: A Tasty Geometry Example
narration: Let us measure a small chocolate box that is 5 cm long, 2 cm wide, and 3 cm high.
First, the base area is 5 times 2, which is 10 square centimeters.
Now, multiply that 10 by the height of 3 to get 30 cubic centimeters.

scenes.title: Quick Recap and Challenge
narration: Remember, area is for flat surfaces and volume is for solid objects.
Area uses square units, while volume uses cubic units.
Think about it: does a flat sticker have volume?

scenes.title: The Curious Market Trip
narration: Aarav is at the market buying a chocolate bar.
The price tag says 25 point 50 rupees.
What does that little dot actually mean?

scenes.title: Parts of a Whole
narration: A decimal dot separates whole numbers from parts.
The first spot is for tenths, like one slice of ten.
The second spot is for hundredths, like one coin of a hundred.

scenes.title: Counting Aarav's Rupees
narration: Aarav has 25 whole rupees in his pocket.
The 50 means 50 paise, which is half a rupee.
So 25 point 50 is just 25 rupees and 50 paise.

scenes.title: Decimals Are Everywhere
narration: Decimals help us measure money, height, and weight perfectly.
Remember, the dot divides whole numbers from smaller parts.
Think about it, how would you write 75 paise using a decimal?

scenes.title: The Grocery Store Mystery
narration: Have you ever felt confused by a long math story at school?
Imagine you are at the market with Aarav buying mangoes.
How do we turn these words into a simple math equation?

scenes.title: Breaking Down The Problem
narration: First, read the story carefully and underline the important numbers.
Next, look for clue words like total, difference, or each.
Total usually means you need to add things together.
If you see the word difference, you probably need to subtract.

scenes.title: Solving Aarav's Mango Problem
narration: Aarav has 50 rupees and buys mangoes for 35 rupees.
We need to find the change left in his pocket.
Fifty minus thirty-five equals fifteen rupees.

scenes.title: Recap And Challenge
narration: Read, identify keywords, and pick the right operation.
Checking your answer helps ensure your math makes sense.
Think about it: what clue words would you use for multiplication?

scenes.title: The Mystery At Home
narration: Aarav is looking for his favorite cricket bat in his messy room.
He knows it is not under his bed or inside his cupboard.
If it is not there, where could it be hiding?

scenes.title: How Logic Works
narration: Logic is like being a detective using clues to find the truth.
We use facts we know to cross out things that are impossible.
What is left standing must be the answer.

scenes.title: Solving The Fruit Puzzle
narration: Priya has an apple, a banana, and a mango in three bowls.
The apple is not in the blue bowl and the mango is in the red bowl.
Since the mango is red, the apple must be in the green bowl.
That leaves the banana for the blue bowl.

scenes.title: Recap And Think
narration: Logic uses facts to clear away guesses.
Always check your clues step by step.
Think about it: If your friend says they are not wearing blue, what colors could they be wearing?

scenes.title: The Fruit Market Mystery
narration: Have you ever wondered which fruit is the most popular in the school canteen?
Arjun counted the fruits sold today to find the answer.
He kept a simple tally to track every single sale.

scenes.title: Reading the Graph
narration: Now Arjun puts his numbers into a tidy bar graph.
The taller the bar, the more fruits were sold that day.
Each square on the side represents one yummy fruit sold.
This helps us see the trends without counting one by one.

scenes.title: Solving the Puzzle
narration: Look at the graph: five students bought apples, but only two bought bananas.
To find the total, we add five plus two to get seven.
It is much faster than counting every single fruit by hand!

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Data helps us organize information so we can compare things quickly.
Remember to always check the labels and the scale on your graph.
Think about it: if you tracked your favorite colors, which color would have the tallest bar?

scenes.title: Spotting Everyday Patterns
narration: Have you noticed the beautiful flowers in Rohan's garden or the tiles on your kitchen floor?
Patterns are designs that repeat in a predictable way.
Why do you think nature and builders love using them so much?

scenes.title: How Patterns Work
narration: Every pattern has a core part called the rule that repeats over and over.
You can find patterns in shapes, colors, numbers, or even sounds.
If you know the rule, you can predict exactly what comes next.

scenes.title: Maths Number Patterns
narration: Let us look at a sequence of numbers: 2, 4, 6, and 8.
The rule here is to add two to the previous number every time.
If we follow the rule, what number comes after eight?
That is right, the next number is ten!

scenes.title: Recap and Think
narration: Patterns are repeating designs based on a specific rule.
They help us organize the world and solve tricky math problems.
Think about it: can you find a pattern in your house today?
